newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian soybean trade resumes after tax protest.
newsitem.headline: Indian soybean trade resumes after tax protest.

text.p: Soybean arrivals in central Indian markets are expected to pick up following the end of an 18-day strike by the trade over the introduction of a local market tax, dealers said on Tuesday.
They said the strike was called off on Monday and soybean arrivals at processing plants, which had been brought to a halt, were gradually picking up.
The central state of Madhya Pradesh, which accounts for about 80 percent of the country's soybean output, has doubled its market tax to two percent with effect from May 1, 1997.
Traders said soymeal was quoted at 13,500 to 13,700 rupees per tonne, compared with about 11,850 to 11,900 a year ago.
Export demand for Indian soymeal was dull because of a lack of availability and high prices, traders said.
Soymeal for export was quoted at $327 to $328 per tonne FAS (free alongside ship), up from about $265 at the same time last year.
Traders said export demand in the rapeseed sector was strong as buyers sought cheaper alternatives to soymeal.
